## Introduction

In this project, we will be analysing the demand for rented bikes in Seoul, with the aims of **predicting the demand for rented bikes in Seoul considering time and weather variables.** This predictive model will be useful for helping to mainting a stable supply for bike renters, as well as help rented bike companies to project revenues in the future.

## Data

### Raw Dataset

The Seoul rented bikes data set has 8760 observations across 13 features. Each observation records details of the date, hourly bike demand, hour of day, temperature, rainfall, snowfall and other time and weather related-variables.

### Cleaning

In the raw data set, a variable called functioning_day was used to signify if the bike-renting system was operational or not. We realised that when functioning_day == "no," all instances of rented_bike_count had a value of 0. As we are interested in the number of rented bikes, this would not be relevant for our goal.

We also used clean_names() to ensure that all variables have in snake_case for simplicity when writing code.

### Key Variables

The key data points from the dataset that we will be considering are: rented_bike_count, hour, temperature_c, humidity_percent, rainfall_mm, snowfall_cm, seasons, holiday and date. Although we are already considering many variables, this will be further simplified during feature engineering.


### Feature Engineering

We ultimately engineered four variables, but one of which will not be used in our linear model, which will be explained in later sections of this report.

hour_holiday — factor that matches an hour of day to whether that day is a holiday or not.

precipitation — has values 1 or 0, used to indicate if there was any forms of rainfall or snowfall.

is_weekend — determines if the day is a weekday or during the weekend.

peak — determines if the hour of day is a peak commuting time. We have defined this to be 7-9am and 5-7pm. This is the engineered variable that will be removed after exploratory data analysis (EDA).
